frontiers.operatingEnvelope: 800V DC bus (650V–920V), 250 kW peak power, 105°C water-glycol coolant, 48 kHz PWM
frontiers.whatChangedRecently: Within the last 90 days, ETH Zurich PES and Fraunhofer IISB demonstrated closed-loop dV/dt active gate-shaping combined with copper-clip double-side sintered Si3N4 AMB substrates (<1.8 nH loop inductance), lifting verified 800V WLTP efficiency to 98.7% at 105°C coolant without violating CISPR 25 Class 5.
frontiers.gapRootCauseAnalysis: At 800V bus voltage and 48 kHz switching frequency, the 1.3% efficiency gap between the customer baseline (97.4%) and the research frontier (98.7%) is dominated by two physical bottlenecks: (1) partial-load turn-on switching energy (E_on) and reverse-recovery capacitive losses during low-torque WLTP urban cruising, and (2) 6.2 nH stray commutation inductance in wire-bonded DBC packaging forcing conservative gate resistance (Rg = 4.7 Ω) to contain CISPR 25 Class 5 EMI.
recommendedNextActions: Transition from hard-switched fixed-Rg gate driving to closed-loop active gate trajectory control (EP4198231A1) to recover +0.6% partial-load WLTP efficiency.
Replace Al-wirebonded AlN substrates with Fraunhofer IISB copper-clip Ag-sintered Si3N4 AMB power modules (<1.8 nH stray inductance).
Execute Milestone 1 & 2 bench validation inside Protected Project Room QRT-RM-800V under Mutual NDA and segregated Background IP.

brainstormRooms.summary: Consensus reached on combining closed-loop active dV/dt feedback with Fraunhofer IISB 1.75 nH Cu-clip packaging to eliminate 58% of turn-on switching energy without exceeding CISPR 25 Class 5 EMI limits.

Run SPICE transient simulation on double-pulse gate driver testbench
Draft mutual NDA and Background IP schedule for project room

messages.content: Welcome team. Our dyno baseline is 97.4% WLTP efficiency on our 800V / 250 kW inverter. We need to reach the 98.7% research frontier to hit OEM targets.

Under low-torque WLTP urban cruising, hard-switching losses dominate. With closed-loop active gate trajectory shaping, we can dynamically boost gate current during switching intervals and clamp Miller plateau ringing.

Cross-referencing the Knowledge Hub: Patent EP4198231A1 and IEEE TPEL 2026 paper show this architecture achieves +0.65% efficiency gain while holding radiated EMI below CISPR 25 Class 5. Recommend launching a SPICE simulation job in the Simulation Hub to verify junction temperatures.
We have tested the Si3N4 AMB substrate with 1.75 nH stray inductance. That allows gate resistance Rg to be reduced from 4.7 Ω down to 1.8 Ω safely.

knowledgeItems.title: Zero-Voltage-Switching and Active Gate Trajectory Control in 800V Automotive Traction Inverters
knowledgeItems.authorsOrOrg: Prof. Dr. Johann W. Kolar, Dr. D. Bortis (ETH Zurich PES)
knowledgeItems.abstract: Presents a condition-aware active gate-shaping circuit topology reducing partial-load switching losses by 58% in 1200V SiC MOSFET bridges under 800V automotive drive cycles, while maintaining strict compliance with CISPR 25 Class 5 radiated EMI.
keyFindings: Eliminates 58% of turn-on energy at partial load torque points
Active Miller clamping suppresses spurious turn-on at 50 V/ns dV/dt
Verified experimentally on 250 kW liquid-cooled dynamometer bench

knowledgeItems.title: AQG 324 — Automotive Qualification Guideline for Power Semiconductor Modules
knowledgeItems.authorsOrOrg: ECPE European Center for Power Electronics
knowledgeItems.abstract: Defines rigorous thermal, mechanical, electrical, and environmental stress requirements for power semiconductor modules deployed in electric and hybrid road vehicle powertrains.
keyFindings: Power cycling lifetime verification requirements under ΔTj = 80K and ΔTj = 100K
Vibration and mechanical shock profile standards up to 30g
Void fraction threshold standards in Ag/Cu sinter layers (<5% area)

knowledgeItems.title: SPICE & PLECS Electro-Thermal Modeling Tutorial: Stray Inductance Extraction in SiC Modules
knowledgeItems.abstract: Step-by-step tutorial on extracting parasitic inductances from 3D CAD step files and integrating frequency-dependent loss models into SPICE and PLECS simulation environments.
keyFindings: Ansys Q3D field solver extraction workflow for 6-pack inverter modules

Automated double-pulse waveform comparison with bench telemetry
